body: Chatham County commissioners adopted a moratorium on new data centers in February 2026 that runs until February 11, 2027, or until new zoning rules are adopted, NC Newsline reported. Eco TIP West plans a 750-megawatt data center at the Triangle Innovation Point West business park near Moncure. It sued the county in Chatham County Superior Court in April, arguing the project was already in progress when the moratorium passed and should be exempt. The company said it had spent $11 million on the project and that the site's zoning allowed a data center, and the North State Journal reported that the county had issued a zoning permit in late October 2025 confirming the use was permitted by right once water and sewer service were available.

The county argued, according to the Carolina Journal, that Eco TIP had no vested right because it never obtained a development approval for a data center, that it did not submit a complete application before the moratorium took effect, and that summary judgment was premature without discovery. After an August 31 hearing, Judge John Morris found 'no genuine issue as to any material fact' and ruled for the developer. The Carolina Journal reported that he awarded attorney's fees and reserved the determination of damages for further proceedings; NC Newsline reported that the county must pay damages for trying to slow the project.
Neither outlet reported whether the county will appeal. NC Newsline said it is unclear how the ruling will affect the other moratoria adopted across the state.

timeline.label: Chatham County issues a zoning permit for the site, according to the North State Journal
Chatham County commissioners adopt a year-long data center moratorium
Eco TIP West sues Chatham County in Superior Court
Hearing on Eco TIP West's motion for summary judgment
Judge John Morris grants summary judgment to Eco TIP West, awards attorney's fees and reserves damages
